cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's just reminded them they were washed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 6:11). Now he puts a line in quotes: "Everything is permissible for me,"

cards.question: Paul answers the line "Everything is permissible for me" with a "but." What's his first point?

answers.text: Allowed isn't always good for you

cards.text: Then Paul says the line AGAIN, with a different "but." Friend, the snooze button is permissible, but hit it nine times and now the snooze button is running your whole morning.

cards.question: The second time, Paul says everything is permissible for him, but he will not be ___ by anything.

cards.text: Next Paul quotes another line: "Food for the stomach and the stomach for food," Sounds neat and tidy. Then here comes another "but."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says food and the stomach will last forever.

cards.text: Then Paul turns from food to the body. He says the body is not intended for sexual immorality.

cards.question: Paul says the body isn't intended for sexual immorality. Who does he say it's for?

cards.text: So why does the body matter that much? Paul points to the day God raised the Lord from the dead by His power.

cards.question: God raised the Lord from the dead by His power. What does Paul say God will do for us?

cards.text: Raised from the DEAD, friend, and here I am still bragging that I got out of a junk drawer. Next Paul asks, "Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?"

cards.question: True or false: Paul says it's fine to take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute.

cards.text: Paul says this is no small thing. He quotes Scripture: "The two will become one flesh." (Genesis 2:24)

cards.question: With "the two will become one flesh" in mind, what does Paul say about a man who unites himself with a prostitute?

answers.text: He is one with her in body
Only she is affected by it

cards.question: Paul flips it around: the one who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in ___.

cards.text: Then Paul gives the command in four words: "Flee from sexual immorality." Not stroll. Not tiptoe. FLEE, like a spider just dropped onto your shoulder!

cards.question: Paul says every other sin a man commits is outside his body. What's different about sexual sin?

answers.text: It is a sin against his own body
It only harms the other person
It is a sin nobody can see

cards.text: Then comes another "Do you not know?" This one is about who is in you.

cards.question: What does Paul call the body of a believer?

answers.text: A temple of the Holy Spirit

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the Holy Spirit in them is someone they got on their own.

cards.text: Then Paul says it quietly: "You are not your own;" He lets that one sit, friend. I'm letting it sit too.

cards.question: Paul tells them they are not their own, because they were ___ at a price.

cards.text: Friend, I got bought for 25 cents out of a closeout bin, and I STILL get emotional about it. Paul doesn't name the price here, but now comes his "Therefore."

cards.question: Since they were bought at a price, what does Paul tell them to do with their body?

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "the two will become one flesh", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "Do you not know?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The snooze joke ends with 'now the snooze button is running your whole morning.' That restates the answer to card 4 ('mastered') in plain words, so the baker is handed the answer instead of reasoning toward it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'So why does the body matter that much? Paul points to the day God raised the Lord' presents verse 14 as Paul's reason for verse 13. The text doesn't state that connection. It also adds 'the day,' which isn't in the text.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Paul says this is no small thing' credits Paul with a statement he doesn't make in 1 Corinthians 6:16. That adds a fact instead of being a storyteller's line.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: 'the Holy Spirit in them' uses 'them' without saying who. The question never names who Paul is talking about.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Paul says it quietly' and 'He lets that one sit' describe how Paul delivers the line. Nothing in the text supports this. The text also shows the opposite: 'You are not your own;' runs straight on into 'you were bought at a price' in the same sentence (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
